summary: A story about a dream and future technology for humanity known as the Space Mission.
details:
The Little Device that Never Returned

Long ago, there once was a girl in a village in this world who saw an image of Mars.

She noticed a peculiar contraption standing all by itself in a red desert.

"Father," she enquired, "what happens to those machines after NASA accomplishes its work? Are they returned home?"

Her father laughed.

"Some are. But most are left behind. And their tales are even more amazing than you think!"

In her dreams that night, the girl was flying into space.

First of all, she landed on the Moon.

There, he found an old landing platform on the Moon, a few instruments, and footprints of astronauts who had walked there a long time ago.

But what caught her eye the most was a little reflective instrument of science.

"Why is this here?" the girl asked in her dream.

And a voice replied.

"I am an Apollo retroreflector. I was left by astronauts to enable scientists on Earth to send lasers towards me to measure the distance between Earth and the Moon. Even today, I still have a story to tell in science."

The girl was amazed.

Her next destination was Mars.

There, she found a splendid rover examining its rocky surroundings. Further away, she found a parachute and a big protective capsule.

"Why did someone leave these here?" the girl asked.

"These helped me land on Mars safely. My parachute slowed down my descent, and my protective capsule provided me with protection while traveling through space. Once their jobs were done, they detached from me."

The girl looked around.

"So these objects are not just rubbish?"

"That’s right," agreed the rover. "These are signs of engineering, bravery, teamwork, and discoveries. Scientists will be able to examine them and learn how well our landing systems worked."

The girl realized something very important all of a sudden.

Each object had its own purpose.

Each landing had its own story.

Each mission had left behind a small fragment of human imagination.

The girl woke up and rushed to see her father.

"Now I know what I want to be when I grow up!" she yelled.

"What do you mean?" asked her father.

"A space explorer! I want to create machines that will fly to other planets and leave behind their stories for future generations to remember."

Her father smiled.

"But remember one thing, my girl. Sometimes the most significant success of a machine is not the distance it travels but how much it teaches us."

The girl asked her father to show some pictures of space waste from her father's mobile.

Her father wondered.

"Do you know, in earlier days, space missions were done with less computational capacity than today's modern mobile phone? That time, though, scientists had limited facilities; they had a willingness to learn the unknown and never give up mindset"

And from that day on, the little girl never looked at an abandoned machine as junk.

For she knew there was a story to be told.

The End.

The lesson from the story

Do not underestimate the value of something that has fulfilled its purpose, because Discoveries of yesterday are the inspirations of tomorrow.
